advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Gate the recency anchor's reviewed_at on the replay actually succeeding (e.g. only stamp coverage.replayed_review when replay produced content / a verified_at_sha), so an empty fail-open reuse does not render a misleading 'last review' timestamp.
evidence: _replay_anchor (reuse.py:107-109) fetches reviewed_at unconditionally: `reviewed_at = sidecar.latest_review_timestamp(...)` `if reviewed_at: anchor["reviewed_at"] = reviewed_at`

test_pass_reuse_degrades_to_empty_on_mismatched_fingerprint (test_plan_review_reuse_replay.py:171-186) asserts only empty advisory/coaching/indeterminate and never checks the anchor content, so this leak is uncovered
advisory.finding: In idempotent_reuse the recency anchor's reviewed_at is populated independently of whether the sidecar content was actually replayed: when _pass_replay fails open to empty lists (mismatched material_fingerprint, contradictory stored BLOCK, or unreadable sidecar), replay['verified_at_sha'] is None so the anchor omits the SHA, but _replay_anchor still fetches latest_review_timestamp and stamps coverage.replayed_review={'reviewed_at': <ts>}. The CLI then prints 'last review: reviewed at <date>' beside an EMPTY PASS result, implying the empty output reflects a review dated then.
scenarios: A stored PASS sidecar exists but its material_fingerprint differs from the current plan; reuse still fires empty but the CLI shows a 'last review: reviewed at ...' line unrelated to the (empty) content

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive reviewed_at from the SAME sidecar payload that supplied the replayed content (e.g. carry the timestamp out of latest_review_result) rather than the independent latest_review_timestamp newest-file scan.
evidence: latest_review_timestamp (sidecar.py:287) `prefix = files[-1].split("-", 1)[0]` — newest file, no schema guard, no walk-back
latest_review_result (sidecar.py:184-196) walks `for fname in reversed(files)` and returns the first payload whose `schema` is v1/v2, tolerating a corrupt/foreign newest file
advisory.finding: The reviewed_at timestamp in the anchor comes from sidecar.latest_review_timestamp, which returns the ns prefix of the NEWEST REVIEW_RESULT file with no schema check and no walk-back, whereas the replayed content and verified_at_sha come from sidecar.latest_review_result, which walks back over malformed/foreign-schema newest files to the first usable v1/v2 payload. When the newest file is unusable/foreign-schema, reviewed_at references a different sidecar than the content actually replayed, so the recency anchor can misreport when the replayed review was earned.
scenarios: A newer REVIEW_RESULT file exists that is malformed or of a future/foreign schema; content is replayed from an older usable payload but reviewed_at reflects the newer unusable file

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert `coverage.counts` is omitted (not present) on the empty-replay paths (mismatched fingerprint / fail-open) in test_plan_review_reuse_replay.py.
evidence: tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse_replay.py:187-189: `out = reuse.idempotent_reuse(...); assert out["advisory"] == [] and out["coaching"] == [] and out["indeterminate"] == []` — no assertion on coverage['counts']
Named violating input: a mismatched-fingerprint sidecar (`material_fingerprint="fp-OTHER"`) yields empty counts; the omit-empty-counts branch is unexercised.
advisory.finding: No test asserts that `idempotent_reuse` OMITS `coverage.counts` when the replay yields empty counts. The added guard `if replay["counts"]: coverage["counts"] = replay["counts"]` (reuse.py:162-163) has an untested false branch: on the mismatched-fingerprint and fail-open paths `_pass_replay` returns `counts={}`, so `coverage` should have no `counts` key — but `test_pass_reuse_degrades_to_empty_on_mismatched_fingerprint` only asserts the advisory/coaching/indeterminate lists are empty, never `"counts" not in out["coverage"]`. A regression that unconditionally wrote an empty `counts` (or wrote garbage) would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_pass_reuse_degrades_to_empty_on_mismatched_fingerprint (and the fail-open test) add `assert "counts" not in out["coverage"]`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a reuse.py-side test: with `latest_review_timestamp -> None` and no stored `verified_at_sha`, assert `"replayed_review" not in out["coverage"]`.
evidence: tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse_replay.py:115: fixture always sets `latest_review_timestamp` to `_TS_NS` — no None-timestamp case
Named violating input: `latest_review_timestamp` returns `None` and the sidecar has no `verified_at_sha`, so the anchor should be omitted from coverage.
advisory.finding: No test covers `_replay_anchor` returning `{}` and the resulting omission of `coverage.replayed_review` on the model side. The added guard `if anchor: coverage["replayed_review"] = anchor` (reuse.py:165-166 and 244-245) is only exercised with anchors present; every reuse test pins `latest_review_timestamp` to a truthy `_TS_NS`. No test drives `latest_review_timestamp -> None` together with an absent `verified_at_sha` to assert `"replayed_review" not in out["coverage"]`. The CLI-side graceful omission is tested (test_render_reuse_omits_absent_anchor_gracefully) but the producer-side omission in reuse.py is not.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that monkeypatches `latest_review_timestamp` to return None and uses a sidecar with `verified_at_sha=None`, asserting the reuse verdict's coverage has no `replayed_review` key.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with a PASS sidecar whose counts omit `advisory_surfaced`, asserting all live advisories replay uncapped.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:83-85: `cap = counts.get("advisory_surfaced"); if isinstance(cap, int): advisory = advisory[:cap]`
tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse_replay.py:70: sidecar counts always carry `"advisory_surfaced": 1` — the missing-cap path is never taken
Named violating input: a PASS sidecar whose `coverage.counts` omits `advisory_surfaced` with two live advisory findings should replay both.
advisory.finding: The uncapped-advisory branch of `_pass_replay` is untested. The added `if isinstance(cap, int): advisory = advisory[:cap]` (reuse.py:83-85) slices only when `advisory_surfaced` is an int; when counts lacks `advisory_surfaced` (or it is non-int), ALL live advisories should replay. Every replay test uses `_pass_sidecar` with `advisory_surfaced=1`, so only the cap-applied branch runs. A regression dropping the `isinstance` guard (always slicing, defaulting cap to 0) would silently swallow all advisories and no test would catch it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a case using `_pass_sidecar` with counts lacking `advisory_surfaced` and assert both `f-surfaced` and `f-overflow` appear in `out["advisory"]`.
